quotes.quote:
When I had money, money, O!
My many friends proved all untrue;
But now I have no money, O!
My friends are real, though very few.
quotes.author: William H. Davies
quotes.title: Money
quotes.context: The speaker discovers that losing money clarifies which friendships are real.
quotes.rightsNote: First published in 1911; public domain in the United States.
quotes.notes: Line breaks, spelling, and punctuation checked against the linked transcription on 2026-09-07.

quotes.quote:
Is there, for honest poverty,
That hangs his head, and a' that;
The coward slave we pass him by,
We dare be poor for a' that.
For a' that, and a' that,
Our toils obscure, and a' that;
The rank is but the guinea's stamp,
The man's the gowd for a' that.
quotes.author: Robert Burns
quotes.title: For a’ that and a’ that
quotes.context: Burns separates human worth from rank and the coinage that certifies it.
quotes.rightsNote: Written in 1795; Robert Burns died in 1796. Public domain in the United States.
quotes.notes: Scots spelling, apostrophes, and line breaks checked against the linked transcription on 2026-09-07.

quotes.quote:
Work—work—work!
My labor never flags;
And what are its wages? A bed of straw,
A crust of bread—and rags.
quotes.author: Thomas Hood
quotes.speaker: The seamstress
quotes.title: The Song of the Shirt
quotes.context: The poem speaks in the voice of an exhausted, impoverished seamstress.
quotes.rightsNote: First published in 1843; Thomas Hood died in 1845. Public domain in the United States.
quotes.notes: Line breaks, em dashes, and punctuation checked against the linked transcription on 2026-09-07.

quotes.quote:
Good folk, I have no coin;
To take were to purloin:
I have no copper in my purse,
I have no silver either,
And all my gold is on the furze
That shakes in windy weather
Above the rusty heather.
quotes.author: Christina Rossetti
quotes.speaker: Laura
quotes.title: Goblin Market
quotes.context: Laura tells the goblin merchants she has no money before they propose another form of payment.
quotes.sourceCitation: Laura’s reply to the goblin merchants
quotes.rightsNote: First published in 1862; Christina Rossetti died in 1894. Public domain in the United States.
quotes.notes: Line breaks and punctuation checked against the linked 1913 edition on 2026-09-07.

quotes.quote:
And he was rich,—yes, richer than a king,—
And admirably schooled in every grace:
In fine, we thought that he was everything
To make us wish that we were in his place.

So on we worked, and waited for the light,
And went without the meat, and cursed the bread;
And Richard Cory, one calm summer night,
Went home and put a bullet through his head.
quotes.author: Edwin Arlington Robinson
quotes.title: Richard Cory
quotes.context: The townspeople contrast Cory’s apparent wealth with their own deprivation, then confront what appearances concealed.
quotes.rightsNote: First published in 1897; public domain in the United States.
quotes.notes: Line breaks, punctuation, and the 1921 printed wording checked against the linked transcription on 2026-09-07.

quotes.quote:
Our lives shall not be sweated from birth until life closes—
Hearts starve as well as bodies; Give us Bread, but give us Roses!
quotes.author: James Oppenheim
quotes.title: Bread and Roses
quotes.context: The poem insists that labor deserves beauty and dignity as well as subsistence.
quotes.rightsNote: First published in 1911; public domain in the United States.
quotes.notes: Capitalization, line breaks, semicolon, and punctuation checked against the linked 1925 printing on 2026-09-07.

quotes.author: Percy Bysshe Shelley
quotes.title: Song to the Men of England
quotes.context: Shelley sets workers’ production against others’ ownership of its results.
quotes.rightsNote: Written in 1819 and first published in 1839; Percy Bysshe Shelley died in 1822. Public domain in the United States.
quotes.notes: Line breaks and punctuation checked against the linked 1914 edition on 2026-09-07.

quotes.quote:
Bowed by the weight of centuries he leans
Upon his hoe, and gazes on the ground;
The emptiness of ages in his face,
And on his back the burden of the world.
quotes.author: Edwin Markham
quotes.title: The Man with the Hoe
quotes.context: Markham’s poem responds to Jean-François Millet’s painting of a field laborer.
quotes.rightsNote: First published in 1899; public domain in the United States.
quotes.notes: Line breaks and punctuation checked against a linked 1900 printing on 2026-09-07.

quotes.quote:
Publication is the auction
Of the mind of man,
Poverty be justifying
For so foul a thing.
quotes.author: Emily Dickinson
quotes.title: Publication is the auction
quotes.context: Dickinson rejects the reduction of thought and spirit to a market price.
quotes.sourceCitation: Stanza 1, Further Poems of Emily Dickinson (1929)
quotes.rightsNote: First published in 1929; public domain in the United States.
quotes.notes: This record preserves the wording and capitalization of the linked 1929 printing, not a later manuscript edition. Checked 2026-09-07.

quotes.quote:
In the Carboniferous Epoch we were promised abundance for all,
By robbing selective Peter to pay for collective Paul;
But, though we had plenty of money, there was nothing our money could buy,
And the Gods of the Copybook Headings said: "If you don't work you die."
quotes.author: Rudyard Kipling
quotes.title: The Gods of the Copybook Headings
quotes.context: Kipling contrasts political promises of abundance with material scarcity.
quotes.rightsNote: First published in 1919; public domain in the United States.
quotes.notes: Line breaks, wording, and quotation marks checked against the linked transcription on 2026-09-07.

quotes.author: Stephen Collins Foster
quotes.title: Hard Times Come Again No More
quotes.context: Foster asks comfortable listeners to attend to the suffering around them.
quotes.sourceCitation: Verse 1; Firth, Pond & Co. sheet music, 1854

quotes.quote:
You will eat, bye and bye,
In that glorious land above the sky;
Work and pray, live on hay,
You'll get pie in the sky when you die.
quotes.author: Joe Hill
quotes.title: The Preacher and the Slave
quotes.context: Hill satirizes promises of future reward offered in place of food and justice in the present.
quotes.sourceCitation: Chorus, Songs of the Workers, 15th edition (1919)
quotes.rightsNote: Published before 1931; public domain in the United States. This record covers the published lyrics, not a later recording.
quotes.notes: Line breaks, spelling, and punctuation checked against the linked 1919 songbook transcription on 2026-09-07.

quotes.quote:
It is we who plowed the prairies; built the cities where they trade.
Dug the mines and built the workshops; endless miles of railroad laid.
Now we stand, outcast and starving, 'mid the wonders we have made;
For the Union makes us strong.
quotes.author: Ralph H. Chaplin
quotes.title: Solidarity Forever!
quotes.context: The verse contrasts workers’ creation of material wealth with their exclusion from it.
quotes.sourceCitation: Verse 3, Songs of the Workers, 15th edition (1919)
quotes.rightsNote: Published before 1931; public domain in the United States. This record covers the published lyrics, not a later recording or arrangement.
quotes.notes: Line breaks, spelling, capitalization, and punctuation checked against the linked 1919 songbook transcription on 2026-09-07.

quotes.quote:
We have fed you all, for a thousand years
And you hail us still unfed,
Though there's never a dollar of all your wealth
But marks the worker's dead.
We have yielded our best to give you rest
And you lie on crimson wool.
Then if blood be the price of all your wealth,
Good God! We have paid it in full.
quotes.author: Unknown Proletarian
quotes.title: We Have Fed You All for a Thousand Years
quotes.context: An anonymous labor lyric measures accumulated wealth against the lives that produced it.
quotes.sourceCitation: Verse 1, Songs of the Workers, 15th edition (1919)
quotes.rightsNote: Anonymous work first published in 1908; public domain in the United States. This record covers the published lyrics, not a later recording.
quotes.notes: Line breaks, spelling, and punctuation checked against the linked 1919 songbook transcription on 2026-09-07.

quotes.quote:
If I never have a cent
I'll be rich as Rockefeller
Gold dust at my feet
On the sunny side of the street
quotes.author: Dorothy Fields and Jimmy McHugh
quotes.title: On the Sunny Side of the Street
quotes.context: The refrain converts material poverty into emotional abundance.
quotes.rightsNote: The 1930 composition and lyrics entered the U.S. public domain on January 1, 2026. Later arrangements and recordings are not included.
quotes.notes: Words and lineation checked against the linked original sheet-music scan on 2026-09-07.

quotes.quote:
‘As I feared....your mother has a dangerous temperature. Get that prescription at once.’
‘It will cost about twenty lire.’
quotes.author: Monckton Hoffe
quotes.speaker: The doctor
quotes.title: Street Angel
quotes.context: Angela learns the price of medicine for her ill mother.
quotes.rightsNote: The 1928 U.S. film is public domain; later scores and restorations are excluded.

quotes.quote:
GOLD - GOLD - GOLD - GOLD
Bright and Yellow, Hard and Cold, Molten, Graven, Hammered, Rolled, Hard to Get and Light to Hold; Stolen, Borrowed, Squandered - Doled.
quotes.author: Erich von Stroheim
quotes.speaker: Opening intertitle, quoting Thomas Hood
quotes.title: Greed
quotes.context: The film opens by framing gold as difficult to gain and easy to lose.

quotes.quote:
You have beauty, charm, money.
You have got money?
If not, we can quit right now.
quotes.author: George S. Kaufman and Morrie Ryskind
quotes.speaker: Captain Jeffrey T. Spaulding
quotes.title: Animal Crackers
quotes.context: Spaulding abruptly reprioritizes a declaration of admiration when money enters the question.

quotes.quote: During the next five years two eventful things happened to the Simses. A baby sister was born....and John received an $8 raise.
quotes.author: King Vidor and John V. A. Weaver
quotes.speaker: Intertitle
quotes.title: The Crowd
quotes.context: A family milestone and a small wage increase receive the same dry narrative weight.
